description_html: Your work days are brighter here.     We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.           About the Team  Your work matters here. At Workday Government, we focus on outcomes that serve a larger mission. Our work supports U.S. federal agencies as they modernize and transform the full employee lifecycle experience and finance operations.   You will join a highly motivated, collaborative engineering team that thrives on teamwork, open communication, and shared problem-solving. Working with modern technologies like Kubernetes, Terraform, and Docker, our goal is to partner closely to build resilient, reliable systems that our customers can depend on. We are looking for driven engineers who take genuine pride in their craft, value strong collaboration across teams, take ownership of initiatives, and consistently deliver impactful outcomes.  The work isn’t theoretical. It’s operational. It’s high-impact. And it demands technical rigor, strong teamwork, and long-term thinking.    About the Role       This role will support one or more direct or indirect contracts with the U.S. Federal Government which, due to federal government security requirements, mandates that all Workday personnel working on the contracts be United States citizens (naturalized or native).          Location Note:     May be required to be on site at client locations in the DC, MD, and VA (DMV) area.     Role Overview:     As a Software Development Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in guiding Workday’s efforts to build, deploy, and scale solutions for our Kubernetes platform in AWS GovCloud. You will lead infrastructure automation, enhance CI/CD pipelines, build robust observability tools, and drive air-gapped deployment methodologies.    You have a growth mindset and thrive in a collaborative, outcome-driven environment where cross-team partnership is key. You will be part of a team promoting a diverse and inclusive culture where you and your teammates are energized, engaged, and excited to solve complex engineering challenges together every day.     Responsibilities:      Platform & Workload Management:  Run, manage, and scale complex containerized workloads on Kubernetes clusters deployed in AWS GovCloud environments.     Infrastructure Automation:  Provision and automate infrastructure, configurations, and deployment pipelines using Terraform, Terragrunt, Docker, AWS, and Argo CD.     Air-Gapped & Secure Deployments:  Design, implement, and maintain air-gapped deployment methodologies to support strict security, compliance, and isolation requirements.     Observability & Reliability:  Build, maintain, and optimize comprehensive monitoring, logging, and alerting systems to ensure high availability and visibility into our managed services.     Distributed Systems Troubleshooting:  Apply deep expertise in troubleshooting distributed systems to quickly diagnose and resolve complex platform, infrastructure, and network issues.     Collaboration & Results:  Work closely with peer development teams, security leaders, and cross-functional partners across multiple locations to deliver reliable, high-impact outcomes.     Security & Compliance:  Implement and maintain enterprise security standards for the platform, ensuring full compliance with federal industry standards.     Knowledge Sharing & Documentation:  Author clear technical documentation, participate in architectural reviews, and actively mentor team members to foster a culture of continuous learning.       About You       Clearance & Eligibility Requirements:     U.S. Citizenship:  Required due to federal government contract requirements.   Security Clearance:  Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government TS/SCI security clearance with CI Polygraph.  An active TS/SCI w/ CI Poly is strongly preferred.        Basic Qualifications (Mid-Level/ P3):      Experience:  3+ years of hands-on experience building, scaling, and maintaining production cloud infrastructure, DevOps pipelines, or platform engineering systems.   Infrastructure as Code:  Proven proficiency (2+ years) with infrastructure automation tools such as Terraform or Terragrunt.   CI/CD & GitOps:  Hands-on experience (2+ years) managing continuous delivery pipelines using tools like Argo CD, Jenkins, or GitLab CI.   Software Development:  Proficiency in (2+ years) modern scripting or programming languages, with a preference for Go or Python.   Technical Leadership:  Demonstrated ability (1+ years) to independently lead technical initiatives, troubleshoot distributed systems, and mentor junior engineers.      Basic Qualifications (Senior/ P4):      Experience:  5+ years of hands-on experience building, scaling, and maintaining production cloud infrastructure, DevOps pipelines, or platform engineering systems.   Infrastructure as Code:  Proven proficiency (3+ years) with infrastructure automation tools such as Terraform or Terragrunt.   CI/CD & GitOps:  Hands-on experience (3+ years) managing continuous delivery pipelines using tools like Argo CD, Jenkins, or GitLab CI.   Software Development:  Proficiency in (3+ years) modern scripting or programming languages, with a preference for Go or Python.   Technical Leadership:  Demonstrated ability (3+ years) to independently lead technical initiatives, troubleshoot distributed systems, and mentor junior engineers.       Other Qualifications (preferred):      Kubernetes & AWS:  Deep production experience managing containerized workloads in AWS (ideally AWS GovCloud) using Kubernetes and Docker.   Air-Gapped Systems:  Practical experience implementing or managing air-gapped deployment methodologies and isolated cloud architectures.   Observability & Telemetry:  Background in building robust monitoring, logging, and alerting systems for distributed platforms (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, etc).   Security & Compliance:  Familiarity with federal security frameworks (e.g., FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, Zero Trust architecture).   Certifications:  DoD 8570/8140 compliance at IAT Level II or higher (e.g., CompTIA Security+, CySA+, CASP+) along with a current Computing Environment credential.   Education:  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent military / practical engineering experience in lieu of a degree).       Workday Pay Transparency Statement      The annualized base salary ranges for the primary location and any additional locations are listed below.  Workday pay ranges vary based on work location. As a part of the total compensation package, this role may be eligible for the Workday Bonus Plan or a role-specific commission/bonus, as well as annual refresh stock grants. Recruiters can share more detail during the hiring process. Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, skills, job duties, and business need, among other things. For more information regarding Workday’s comprehensive benefits, please   click here  .      Primary Location: USA.VA.Reston    Primary Location Base Pay Range:  $137,000 USD - $205,400 USD    Additional US Location(s) Base Pay Range: $123,900 USD - $222,000 USD    Our Approach to Flexible Work      With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. We know that flexibility can take shape in many ways, so rather than a number of required days in-office each week, we simply   spend at least half (50%) of our time each quarter in the office or in the field   with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter. description_html: Solution Architect Program Manager    Description -    Job Summary   The Solution Architect Program Manager is responsible for driving advanced technology solutions from early concept through architecture definition, proof of concept, productization planning, system integration, validation, and launch readiness. This role combines deep technical capability with disciplined program execution to ensure that innovative concepts are translated into clear scope, committed deliverables, product milestones, and launch timelines.  This position requires strong solution architecture judgment, structured planning, and cross-functional leadership across engineering, product, hardware, firmware, software, validation, security, operations, and external partners. The role owns the bridge between concept feasibility and production execution by defining requirements, aligning stakeholders, managing schedules, resolving technical dependencies, tracking risks, and maintaining readiness documentation required to deliver solutions on product milestones and market launch commitments.     Responsibilities    Drive end-to-end solution programs from concept exploration, business and technical feasibility, architecture definition, POC execution, productization planning, system integration, validation, and launch readiness.  Translate ambiguous innovation concepts into clear solution scope, use cases, requirements, architecture assumptions, success criteria, milestones, resource needs, and execution plans.  Own integrated schedules that align engineering deliverables with product development checkpoints, POR decisions, validation gates, manufacturing readiness, and launch timeline commitments.  Partner closely with product management, system architecture, hardware, firmware, software, security, validation, operations, and external suppliers to manage dependencies and secure delivery commitments.  Lead architecture and technical tradeoff discussions to ensure solution designs are scalable, secure, manufacturable, supportable, and aligned with product roadmap priorities.  Define and maintain program artifacts, including functional requirements, interface assumptions, system-state definitions, delivery plans, issue logs, risk registers, decision records, validation plans, and readiness checklists.  Drive issue triage, dependency closure, technical decision-making, mitigation planning, fallback options, and escalation paths to keep programs on schedule.  Review program deliverables for alignment with solution intent, architecture requirements, product milestone criteria, quality expectations, security standards, and production-readiness needs.  Communicate program status, risks, tradeoffs, decision asks, recovery plans, and launch readiness clearly to engineering leaders, product stakeholders, and executive audiences.  Enable successful transition of innovation solutions into scalable product programs that can be delivered on committed commercial product milestones and launch timelines.      Education & Experience Recommended    Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related technical discipline.  10+ years of experience in solution architecture, system software, embedded software, firmware, platform engineering, technical program management, or complex hardware/software product development.  Proven experience driving technical solutions from concept or POC through architecture alignment, productization planning, integration, validation, production readiness, and product launch.      Preferred Certifications   Solution Architecture & Productization Leadership   Experience defining solution architecture, feature scope, system boundaries, technical assumptions, and integration models for new technology programs.  Ability to convert early concepts into executable productization plans with clear scope, milestones, dependencies, exit criteria, risks, and launch-readiness requirements.  Experience managing roadmap alignment, agile execution, backlog priorities, release readiness, issue triage, defect tracking, and executive status reporting.   Technical Depth, Integration, and Launch Readiness   Strong familiarity with embedded systems, firmware, drivers, operating system interfaces, connectivity, security, manageability, validation, and commercial PC platform integration.  Experience coordinating hardware, firmware, software, validation, manufacturing, and supplier dependencies required to move solutions from lab feasibility into product programs.  Exposure to AI-enabled device experiences, edge AI, device orchestration, intelligent endpoint platforms, or commercial PC innovation is preferred.      Knowledge & Skills    Deep technical understanding of solution architecture, system integration, embedded platforms, PC architecture, embedded software, drivers, kernel-level software, operating system interfaces, connectivity, security, manageability, and validation practices.  Hands-on knowledge of embedded software and system software development, including C/C++, Python or scripting languages, RTOS or Linux/Windows system concepts, device drivers, firmware interfaces, boot flows, power management, performance optimization, and hardware/software debugging.  Experience with software development lifecycle practices for embedded and system software, including requirements definition, design reviews, source control, CI/CD pipelines, unit and integration testing, defect triage, code quality, security reviews, and release readiness.  Ability to work across low-level platform software and higher-level solution architecture to evaluate technical feasibility, identify integration gaps, debug cross-domain issues, and guide engineering teams toward production-quality implementation.  Strong ability to define scope, structure ambiguous concepts, identify technical gaps, sequence workstreams, and drive execution from concept to productization.  Skilled in milestone planning, integrated schedule management, dependency tracking, risk mitigation, issue triage, fallback planning, and release-readiness governance.  Ability to facilitate architecture reviews, technical tradeoff discussions, design decisions, and cross-functional alignment across engineering and product teams.  Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to summarize technical risks, schedule impacts, decision asks, recovery options, and launch-readiness status.  Familiarity with agile planning, CI/CD workflows, defect tracking tools, source control processes, validation planning, system debugging, and supplier-delivery management.      Cross-Org Skills  • Effective Communication • Results Orientation • Learning Agility • Digital Fluency • Customer Centricity   Impact & Scope  • Impacts large functions and leads large, cross-division functional teams or projects.   Complexity  • Provides highly innovative solutions to complex problems within established policy.   Disclaimer  • This job description describes the general nature and level of work performed in this role. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, skills, responsibilities, knowledge, etc. These may be subject to change and additional functions may be assigned as needed by management.     The pay range for this role is  $147,050  to  $230,850  USD annually with additional opportunities for pay in the form of bonus and/or equity (applies to United States of America candidates only). Pay varies by work location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.
